description: Reference knowledge pack. The Go analyzer defines its rules in internal/analyzer; TestRulesJSON_MatchesAnalyzer keeps the ids, categories and remediation ids here identical to the analyzer. Spark / unified-memory rules (docs/roadmap/spark-support.md section 5, catalog docs/roadmap/spark-rules.json) carry platforms (closed set dgx-spark, rtx-spark, jetson, grace-hopper, arm64-dgpu, all), impact (none | reversible | persistent | irreversible | data-loss: the most invasive next step), verbatim next_steps (state-changing steps start with 'Advisory' and name the revert command; read-only steps always come first), source_ids (Sn of spark-support.md section 13) and sources (URLs). Every rule carries impact.

rules.title: No NVIDIA GPU Detected
rules.description: No NVIDIA GPU was found in the system inventory.

rules.title: Hybrid GPU Configuration Detected
rules.description: Both NVIDIA and integrated graphics detected.

rules.title: NVIDIA Driver Version Not Detected
rules.description: nvidia-smi did not return a driver version.

rules.title: nvidia-smi Not Found in PATH
rules.description: The nvidia-smi utility was not found.

rules.title: NVIDIA Jetson Detected
rules.description: The host is an NVIDIA Jetson / Tegra board (/etc/nv_tegra_release present or the device-tree model names a Jetson). nvidia-smi does not exist on Tegra, so no-nvidia-gpu, driver-not-detected and nvidia-smi-missing are suppressed and GPU, thermal and PCIe diagnostics are limited; tegrastats and jetson_release are the native tools.

rules.title: Display Driver Resets Detected (Event ID 4101)
rules.description: Event ID 4101 indicates the display driver stopped responding and was recovered by Windows (confidence 92 and CRIT at 3+ events in 30 days).

rules.title: nvlddmkm Driver Errors Detected
rules.description: nvlddmkm kernel-mode driver errors detected (confidence 92 and CRIT at 5+ events in 30 days).

rules.title: Corrected Hardware Errors Logged (WHEA)
rules.description: Corrected WHEA events (ECC, PCIe retry) in the last 30 days. Escalates to WARN when an event names the NVIDIA GPU or its bus (confidence 75) or at 50+ events (confidence 70).

rules.title: Uncorrected Hardware Errors (WHEA)
rules.description: Uncorrected WHEA events (fatal machine check, PCIe or memory errors) were logged in the last 30 days; these cause bugchecks, freezes and data corruption.

rules.title: Power Plan Not Set to High Performance
rules.description: Balanced or Power Saver plans may throttle performance.

rules.title: Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS) is Enabled
rules.description: HAGS is explicitly enabled; it can cause stuttering in certain games or driver versions.

rules.title: Recent Windows Updates Installed
rules.description: Windows Updates installed in the last 60 days while driver resets were also logged; updates can occasionally introduce driver compatibility issues.

rules.title: NVIDIA App / GeForce Experience Detected
rules.description: NVIDIA overlay software detected.

rules.title: Overlay/Recording Software Detected
rules.description: Multiple overlays can compete for resources.

rules.title: No NVIDIA GPU Available for Hardware Encoding
rules.description: NVIDIA GPU not detected — hardware encoding is not available.

rules.title: Nouveau Driver is Active (Instead of NVIDIA)
rules.description: The open-source nouveau driver is loaded instead of proprietary NVIDIA.

rules.title: NVIDIA Kernel Module Not Loaded
rules.description: The nvidia kernel module is not loaded and nvidia-smi reports no driver version.

rules.title: No /dev/nvidia* Device Nodes Found
rules.description: NVIDIA module loaded but device nodes are missing.

rules.title: libcuda.so Not Found
rules.description: libcuda.so could not be located.

rules.title: DKMS Build Failure Detected
rules.description: DKMS failed to build NVIDIA modules for current kernel.

rules.title: Secure Boot Enabled — NVIDIA Module May Be Blocked
rules.description: Secure Boot is on and NVIDIA module is not loaded.

rules.title: Secure Boot Enabled — NVIDIA Module is Loading Successfully
rules.description: Secure Boot is on and module signing is configured correctly.

rules.title: CUDA Toolkit Newer Than Driver Supports
rules.description: The CUDA toolkit's major version is newer than the driver's CUDA runtime; programs built with it fail with 'CUDA driver version is insufficient'.

rules.title: CUDA Toolkit Minor Version Newer Than Driver
rules.description: The CUDA toolkit is a newer minor release than the driver's CUDA runtime within the same major; minor-version compatibility usually makes this work.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA Build Newer Than Driver
rules.description: The PyTorch wheel's CUDA runtime is newer than the driver supports and torch.cuda.is_available() is False; suggests the nearest published wheel tag.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA Build Newer Than Driver (working)
rules.description: The PyTorch wheel's CUDA major is ahead of the driver's but torch.cuda.is_available() is True, most likely via a forward-compatibility package.

rules.title: PyTorch Import Error
rules.description: PyTorch could not be imported.

rules.title: PyTorch Installed Without CUDA Support
rules.description: CPU-only PyTorch build detected.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA Available but GPU Not Accessible
rules.description: PyTorch has CUDA compiled in but torch.cuda.is_available() is False for a reason other than a CUDA build newer than the driver.

rules.title: PyTorch CUDA is Working
rules.description: PyTorch GPU acceleration is functional.

rules.title: TensorFlow Import Error
rules.description: TensorFlow could not be imported.

rules.title: TensorFlow Cannot See GPU
rules.description: TensorFlow detected no GPU devices.

rules.title: TensorFlow GPU is Working
rules.description: TensorFlow GPU acceleration is functional.

rules.title: WSL2 GPU Device (/dev/dxg) Not Found
rules.description: /dev/dxg missing in WSL2 environment.

rules.title: WSL2: /dev/dxg Exists but nvidia-smi Fails
rules.description: GPU device exists but NVIDIA tools are misconfigured in WSL2.

rules.title: Low VRAM Detected
rules.description: An NVIDIA GPU has less than 4 GB VRAM (one aggregated finding for all such GPUs).

rules.title: GPU Thermal Throttling Active
rules.description: A thermal slowdown bit (sw_thermal_slowdown / hw_thermal_slowdown) is active in clocks_event_reasons.

rules.title: GPU Running at Its Power Limit
rules.description: Only sw_power_cap is active: the driver holds clocks at the configured power limit, which is normal under sustained load.

rules.title: GPU Clock Slowdown Active
rules.description: A hardware slowdown or power-brake reason (hw_slowdown, hw_power_brake_slowdown) is active, alone or with sw_power_cap; the fix is cabling and PSU, not cooling.

rules.title: GPU Running Hot
rules.description: GPU temperature is 85°C or higher without an active thermal slowdown (WARN); 93°C or higher is CRIT with confidence 90.

rules.title: GPU Fan Not Spinning at Elevated Temperature
rules.description: Fan speed is 0% while GPU temperature exceeds 60°C on a card that reports a fan.

rules.title: PCIe Link Speed Downshifted Under Load
rules.description: PCIe link generation is below maximum while the GPU shows evidence of load (active P-state or utilization).

rules.title: PCIe Link Width Reduced
rules.description: The PCIe link negotiated fewer lanes than the slot and card support. Lane width does not drop at idle, so this points at seating, slot or riser problems.

rules.title: PCIe Link Power-Saving at Idle (expected)
rules.description: PCIe link generation is below maximum but the GPU was idle (or showed no evidence of load); link power management is expected, re-check under load.

rules.title: Mixed Refresh Rate Multi-Monitor Setup
rules.description: Monitors with different refresh rates detected — can cause frame pacing issues.

rules.title: High Display Chain Complexity
rules.description: 3+ monitors on the same GPU may affect gaming performance.

rules.title: High Network Jitter Detected
rules.description: Network jitter exceeds 15ms — may cause lag and stutter in online applications. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Ping Blocked but Network Reachable
rules.description: Every ping probe was lost while DNS resolution succeeded, so ICMP is filtered by a firewall, VPN or cloud network rather than the link losing packets. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Packet Loss Detected
rules.description: Network packet loss detected (CRIT above 5%). Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Wi-Fi Congestion Likely
rules.description: Connected on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi (confidence 75 when the signal is below -70 dBm). Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Slow DNS Resolution
rules.description: DNS resolution exceeds 100ms. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: NVIDIA Xid Errors Detected
rules.description: GPU hardware errors (Xid) found in kernel logs.

rules.title: Software Rendering (llvmpipe) Active
rules.description: GPU is not being used for rendering — falling back to CPU-based llvmpipe.

rules.title: Wayland Session with NVIDIA — Known Compatibility Issues
rules.description: Wayland + NVIDIA can cause screen tearing, window glitches, and application crashes.

rules.title: GPU Stuck in Low Power State Under Load
rules.description: GPU is in P5 or lower while utilization is 60% or higher — the driver or power management is holding clocks down.

rules.title: Ping Produced No Samples
rules.description: Traceroute produced hops but ping returned no samples, so latency, jitter and packet loss could not be measured and no network-quality verdict is possible. ICMP echo is often blocked by firewalls or security software. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: Network Appears Healthy
rules.description: Local network and LAN appear healthy. If experiencing online issues, they may be upstream or service-side. Only evaluated when --network was passed.

rules.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10) Detected
rules.trigger: Linux aarch64 AND (/etc/dgx-release DGX_NAME="DGX Spark" OR nvidia-smi name "NVIDIA GB10" OR lspci [10de:2e12] at 000f:01:00.0 (captured in S23/S12) OR DMI product_name NVIDIA_DGX_Spark)
rules.evidence_template: GB10 platform: {vendor} {model} ({fe_or_oem}); GPU {gpu} CC {cc}; kernel {kernel}; DGX OS {swbuild} / OTA {ota}.
rules.why_it_matters: Enables unified-memory suppressions and DGX OS pairing rules; OEM units lag NVIDIA OTAs.
next_steps: No action; memory comes from /proc/meminfo, nvidia-smi memory fields are expected to be [N/A].
rules.description: Enables unified-memory suppressions and DGX OS pairing rules; OEM units lag NVIDIA OTAs.

rules.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark (N1X) Detected
rules.trigger: Windows host ARM64 AND PNPDeviceID PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_2E03|2E06 (or Name contains "RTX Spark")
rules.evidence_template: RTX Spark N1X ({cores}-core, DEV_{devid}), Windows build {build} ARM64, {oem_model}, pool {ram_gib} GiB (Win32_OperatingSystem.TotalVisibleMemorySize).
rules.why_it_matters: Unified memory and Windows-on-Arm change what nvidia-smi, AdapterRAM (uint32) and CUDA report.
next_steps: Report total RAM as the GPU pool; record driver version and INF.
rules.description: Unified memory and Windows-on-Arm change what nvidia-smi, AdapterRAM (uint32) and CUDA report.

rules.title: NVIDIA Grace Hopper / Grace Blackwell Detected
rules.trigger: aarch64 AND nvidia-smi name contains GH200/GB200/GB300 AND memory.total numeric
rules.evidence_template: {gpu}, {vram_mib} MiB HBM, CC {cc}, NUMA nodes {numa}.
rules.why_it_matters: Coherent memory but real HBM, ECC, BMC; GB10 suppressions must not apply.
next_steps: Apply standard datacenter rules.
rules.description: Coherent memory but real HBM, ECC, BMC; GB10 suppressions must not apply.

rules.title: Unified Memory: nvidia-smi Memory Fields Are [N/A] by Design
rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND (memory.total/used/free == [N/A] OR table Memory-Usage == "Not Supported")
rules.evidence_template: nvidia-smi memory '{value}' on {gpu} is expected on unified-memory iGPUs. Pool: MemTotal {total_gib} GiB measured from /proc/meminfo; the remainder of the 128 GiB LPDDR5X (marketed as 128 GB) is reserved for display/firmware (~8.3 GiB on 2025 units; the 2 GB / 4 GB display reserve is a BIOS toggle since July 2026, S4). MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB, swap {swap_gib} GiB. Fan, power limit, memory clock and PCIe gen/width are also [N/A] or misreported ('GEN 1@ 1x', S7).
rules.why_it_matters: Suppresses low-vram, fan, power-limit and PCIe false alarms; cudaMemGetInfo also under-reports.
next_steps: Use /proc/meminfo MemAvailable (+SwapFree), free -h 'available' or the DGX Dashboard (http://localhost:11000).
rules.description: Suppresses low-vram, fan, power-limit and PCIe false alarms; cudaMemGetInfo also under-reports.

rules.title: Unified Memory Pool Under Pressure
rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND a GPU process is present AND (MemAvailable < 8 GiB = WARN, < 4 GiB = CRIT) OR /proc/pressure/memory full avg10 > 0.1 (WARN) / > 1.0 (CRIT). Thresholds are inferences aligned with the llm-plan OS floor F = 8 GiB so a plan the wizard accepts does not WARN in run. vLLM pre-allocation (--gpu-memory-utilization) intentionally drives MemAvailable low, so PSI is the thrash signal, not MemAvailable alone.
rules.evidence_template: MemAvailable {avail_gib} of {total_gib} GiB; PSI full avg10 {psi}; GPU processes {n}. (A vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM server pre-allocates its fraction of the pool at start-up: low MemAvailable with PSI ~0 is expected while it serves.)
rules.why_it_matters: GPU exhaustion is system RAM exhaustion: OOM killer, frozen SSH or log-less hard reset.
next_steps: Lower vLLM --gpu-memory-utilization (<= 0.85), --max-model-len and --max-num-seqs, or stop other model servers (ports 8000/30000/11434/8355); re-check MemAvailable after the server has finished loading (no system change).
Optional (root only, transient, momentarily slows I/O while caches refill): sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'.
rules.description: GPU exhaustion is system RAM exhaustion: OOM killer, frozen SSH or log-less hard reset.

rules.title: Swap in Use on the Unified Memory Pool
rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND swap used (SwapTotal - SwapFree, incl. zram) >= 1 GiB or > 2% of MemTotal, or /proc/vmstat pswpin grows between the collector samples, while a GPU process is present: INFO. WARN only when in addition MemAvailable < 8 GiB (or PSI full avg10 > 0.1). A few hundred MB of cold pages on the DGX OS default ~15-16 GiB swapfile (S124) never fires.
rules.evidence_template: Swap in use: {used_gib} of {total_gib} GiB ({device}); MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB; vm.swappiness={sw}; pswpin delta {pswpin}. Single user measurement on GB10 (S36): 6.7 GiB swapped cost 43% tok/s, 13 GiB cost 95%.
rules.why_it_matters: Paging the shared pool collapses decode throughput and can hang the box; one community measurement (S36) showed 43-95% token/s loss. Never turn swap off while the workload that filled it is still running.
next_steps: Reduce the footprint first: lower --gpu-memory-utilization / --max-model-len / concurrency or stop other model servers; re-check once the workload is stopped (no system change).
Do not run swapoff while the workload is loaded: with several GiB swapped it fails (ENOMEM) or forces OOM kills of the running model server.
Advisory: after stopping the workload, and only on dedicated inference hosts: sudo swapoff -a (reversible: sudo swapon -a; not persistent across reboot).
Advisory: (persistent, optional) commenting the swap line out of /etc/fstab or masking the swapfile unit survives reboot; revert by restoring the line and running sudo swapon -a.
Advisory: sudo sysctl vm.swappiness=1 (reversible: sudo sysctl vm.swappiness=60; persistent only if written to /etc/sysctl.d/).
rules.description: Paging the shared pool collapses decode throughput and can hang the box; one community measurement (S36) showed 43-95% token/s loss. Never turn swap off while the workload that filled it is still running.

rules.title: Page Cache Holding Unified Memory (reclaimable)
rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND MemFree < 4 GiB AND MemAvailable - MemFree > 20 GiB
rules.evidence_template: MemFree {free_gib} GiB but MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB: {cache_gib} GiB of reclaimable page cache (expected after loading a model with mmap; the kernel reclaims it on demand).
rules.why_it_matters: Informational: page cache is reclaimable by design and fires on any healthy Spark after an mmap model load. NVIDIA's known-issues page (S3) suggests dropping caches only if cudaMalloc fails while MemAvailable is still large.
next_steps: No action unless an allocation failed while MemAvailable was large.
Optional (root only, transient, momentarily slows I/O): sudo sh -c 'sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches' then restart the application (S3).
rules.description: Informational: page cache is reclaimable by design and fires on any healthy Spark after an mmap model load. NVIDIA's known-issues page (S3) suggests dropping caches only if cudaMalloc fails while MemAvailable is still large.

rules.title: Out-of-Memory Events on the Unified Memory Pool
rules.trigger: UnifiedMemory AND kernel log 'Out of memory: Killed process' (WARN) or 'NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY]' (CRIT)
rules.evidence_template: {n_oom} OOM-killer events (last {comm}), {n_nvrm} NVRM NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY events; MemAvailable {avail_gib} GiB, swap used {swap_gib} GiB.
rules.why_it_matters: On GB10 these RM failures preceded log-less hard resets with no Xid trail.
next_steps: Keep >= 8 GiB MemAvailable (the llm-plan floor) and lower --gpu-memory-utilization / context / concurrency (no system change).
Run heavy jobs in a transient scope: systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=100G -p MemorySwapMax=0 <cmd> (no persistent change; S33).

Advisory: updating to driver >= 580.159.03 through the DGX Dashboard (July 2026 OTA with improved OOM handling, S4) replaces driver and GSP firmware packages; OTA updates are not designed to be rolled back, so use the Dashboard path and back up first.
rules.description: On GB10 these RM failures preceded log-less hard resets with no Xid trail.

rules.title: GB10 GPU Missing: GSP Firmware Initialization Failed
rules.trigger: lspci [10de:2e12] AND nvidia-smi 'No devices were found' AND dmesg 'Timeout after 6s of waiting for RPC response from GPU0 GSP' / 'ksec2PrepareBootCommands_GB20B: SEC2 secure boot partition timed out' / 'RmInitAdapter: Cannot initialize GSP firmware RM' / Xid 119
rules.evidence_template: GPU at 000f:01:00.0 but nvidia-smi 'No devices were found'; dmesg '{line}'; nvidia-driver-580-open {drv}, nvidia-firmware-580 {fw}, OTA {ota}, kernel {kernel}.
rules.why_it_matters: Driver and GSP firmware are paired per OTA; a plain apt upgrade (580.173.02 on OTA2607 = 580.159.03) leaves the GPU unbootable.
next_steps: Read-only first: sudo nvidia-spark-ota-check summary shows the torn component; collect sudo nvidia-bug-report.sh before changing anything.
If it persists, open a support case with the bug report (do not reimage as a first step).

Advisory: re-run the DGX Dashboard update (http://localhost:11000), or sudo apt update && sudo apt dist-upgrade && sudo fwupdmgr refresh && sudo fwupdmgr upgrade && sudo reboot (S13). This reinstalls driver packages (revert: apt install the previous versions) and flashes firmware capsules, which cannot be rolled back; unplug AC for 30 s after the firmware step.

Advisory: if the GPU is still missing, downgrade to the OTA-paired driver: sudo apt install nvidia-driver-580-open=<paired> nvidia-firmware-580-<paired> (revert: apt install the newer version again), then sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-580-open (revert: sudo apt-mark unhold nvidia-driver-580-open) and reboot.
rules.description: Driver and GSP firmware are paired per OTA; a plain apt upgrade (580.173.02 on OTA2607 = 580.159.03) leaves the GPU unbootable.

rules.title: DGX OS OTA Is Torn (driver/firmware pairing broken)
rules.trigger: DGX OS AND (nvidia-spark-ota-check torn > 0 OR failed list non-empty OR nvidia-driver-580-open version != nvidia-firmware-580-* version OR linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-$(uname -r) missing)
rules.evidence_template: OTA {name} torn={torn}, failed {failed}; driver pkg {drv} vs firmware pkg {fw}; modules for {kernel}: {state}.
rules.why_it_matters: noble-updates ships newer 580 drivers before the OTA pairs them: GSP failure at next boot or a looping Dashboard update.
next_steps: Prefer Dashboard updates and let them finish; read-only check: sudo nvidia-spark-ota-check summary.

Advisory: if the same update keeps re-appearing, sudo apt install nvidia-firmware-580-<expected-version> and reboot; this replaces the GSP firmware package to match the OTA-paired driver (revert: apt install the previous nvidia-firmware-580-<version>); back up first (S38).
rules.description: noble-updates ships newer 580 drivers before the OTA pairs them: GSP failure at next boot or a looping Dashboard update.

rules.title: Driver Too Old for GB10 (R580 / CUDA 13 required)
rules.trigger: GB10 AND driver major < 580 or nvidia-smi CUDA Version 12.x
rules.evidence_template: Driver {driver} / CUDA {cuda}; GB10 requires R580 open modules and CUDA 13 (signature on the wrong driver: ~5 W and 0% utilization under load).
rules.why_it_matters: sm_121 is unsupported by pre-580 drivers; workloads silently run on CPU.
next_steps: Advisory: update via the DGX Dashboard (Settings > Updates) or sudo apt update && sudo apt dist-upgrade && sudo fwupdmgr refresh && sudo fwupdmgr upgrade && sudo reboot; this replaces the driver (revert: apt install the previous version) and flashes firmware capsules, which cannot be rolled back.

Advisory: (data loss) Last resort, only if a manual driver install left apt unrecoverable: the System Recovery image (docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgx-spark/system-recovery.html, S121) ERASES ALL DATA on the unit; back up first.
rules.description: sm_121 is unsupported by pre-580 drivers; workloads silently run on CPU.

rules.title: Driver Branch Not Supported on DGX Spark
rules.trigger: GB10 AND driver major in {590, 595}
rules.evidence_template: Driver {driver}: NVIDIA staff (aniculescu, 2026-06-08, S40) wrote 'Driver 595 is not yet supported on DGX Spark'; 590.48.01 (CUDA 13.1, via noble-proposed) left ~93 GB of unified memory resident after a vLLM exit in one report (S125; S11 also notes the leak).
rules.why_it_matters: Outside NVIDIA validation; breaks OTA pairing.
next_steps: Advisory: return to the OTA-paired 580.x via the DGX Dashboard (driver downgrade; revert by reinstalling the 590/595 package, which stays unsupported); reboot afterwards.
rules.description: Outside NVIDIA validation; breaks OTA pairing.

rules.title: Foreign NVIDIA Driver Packages on DGX Spark
rules.trigger: GB10 AND dpkg lists any of: nvidia-driver-*-server, nvidia-dkms-*-server (e.g. nvidia-dkms-580-open-server), nvidia-fabricmanager-*, nvidia-nvswitch-*, nvidia-system-station, a non-'-open' nvidia-driver-NNN (nvidia-driver-580, nvidia-driver-570), or the .run installer marker /usr/bin/nvidia-uninstall; or nvidia-smi 'NVIDIA-GB10 not supported'. Excluded on purpose: nvidia-dkms-NNN-open (pulled in by Ubuntu's nvidia-driver-NNN-open metapackage, so a stock unit may carry it) and Ubuntu version suffixes (0ubuntu0.24.04.1, 0ubuntu1 and OEM rebuilds vary); a suffix other than -0ubuntu0.24.04.* is INFO evidence only, until the field kit confirms dpkg -l 'nvidia-dkms*' on a stock unit.
rules.evidence_template: Installed {pkgs}; expected nvidia-driver-580-open + nvidia-firmware-580-<ver> + linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-<kernel> (S11, S30). nvidia-smi '{err}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Spark has no NVSwitch, so fabricmanager/nvswitch packages are wrong; Secure Boot rejects unsigned DKMS modules; -server branches are not paired with the GSP firmware. The S30 case was closed with a System Recovery image, which erases the unit - that is a last resort, not the first step.
next_steps: Read-only: dpkg -l | grep -E 'nvidia-driver|nvidia-dkms|nvidia-fabricmanager|nvidia-nvswitch' and sudo nvidia-spark-ota-check summary to list what differs from the image set.

Advisory: remove only the foreign packages (sudo apt purge <pkgs>) and reinstall the image driver set (sudo apt install nvidia-driver-580-open nvidia-firmware-580-<ver> linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-$(uname -r)), then reboot; revert by reinstalling the removed packages.

Advisory: (data loss) Last resort, only if the driver set cannot be restored: the System Recovery image (docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgx-spark/system-recovery.html, S121) ERASES ALL DATA on the unit; back up first.
rules.description: Spark has no NVSwitch, so fabricmanager/nvswitch packages are wrong; Secure Boot rejects unsigned DKMS modules; -server branches are not paired with the GSP firmware. The S30 case was closed with a System Recovery image, which erases the unit - that is a last resort, not the first step.

rules.title: cuBLAS/cuDNN Batch Failure on DGX Spark (driver bug)
rules.trigger: GB10 AND supplied logs contain 'CUDNN_FE failure 11: CUDNN_BACKEND_API_FAILED' or 'CUBLAS failure 14: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR' (WARN). The v1 version-only INFO variant (driver < 580.173.02) is dropped until 580.173.02 ships in an OTA: spec 2.1 records that pulling it from apt ahead of the OTA broke OTA2607 units.
rules.evidence_template: Log '{line}' on driver {driver}; reported fixed in 580.173.02 (forum report S41, not yet paired by an OTA).
rules.why_it_matters: Batch inference crashes; the fix must arrive via a pairing OTA, not plain apt (see dgx-spark-gsp-init-failure).
next_steps: Until then reduce batch size or use --enforce-eager where the failing kernel is selected (no system change).
Advisory: update through the DGX Dashboard when it offers >= 580.173.02 (driver + firmware change; OTA updates are not designed to be rolled back); do not pull the driver from apt ahead of the OTA.
rules.description: Batch inference crashes; the fix must arrive via a pairing OTA, not plain apt (see dgx-spark-gsp-init-failure).

rules.title: DGX Spark Not Running the -nvidia Kernel
rules.trigger: GB10 AND uname -r does not match ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+-\d+-nvidia(-64k|-lowlatency)?$ (PlatformInfo.NvidiaKernelFlavour false)
rules.evidence_template: Kernel {kernel}; DGX Spark expects Canonical's linux-nvidia flavour (6.14.0-NNNN-nvidia / 6.17.0-NNNN-nvidia).
rules.why_it_matters: Generic kernels lack r8127, mt7925e, GB10 patches and signed NVIDIA modules.
next_steps: Boot the installed -nvidia kernel from the GRUB menu (reversible: pick the other entry next boot).

Advisory: sudo apt install linux-nvidia-hwe-24.04 installs a kernel and modules (revert: select the previous kernel in GRUB, then apt remove the added linux-image-*-nvidia / linux-modules-nvidia-580-open-* packages); reboot afterwards.
rules.description: Generic kernels lack r8127, mt7925e, GB10 patches and signed NVIDIA modules.

rules.title: DGX OS OTA Outdated
rules.trigger: DGX OS AND (DGX_OTA_VERSION < 7.5.0 OR kernel < 6.17 OR driver < 580.159.03); the kernel clause is suppressed when cx7-not-enumerated's 6.17.0-1021/1029 regression variant fired on this host (its stop-gap is an older kernel).
rules.evidence_template: OTA {ota} ({date}), kernel {kernel}, driver {driver}; current FE stack DGX OS 7.5.0 / 580.159.03 / CUDA 13.0.2 / kernel 6.17.
rules.why_it_matters: Older OTAs: 6.14 mmap regression, Vulkan broken on 580.95.05, CX-7 power fixes, OOM handling (580.159.03).
next_steps: Advisory: update via DGX Dashboard (Settings > Updates); OEM units via the OEM channel. An OTA replaces driver, kernel and firmware capsules and is not designed to be rolled back; back up first and keep the unit on AC for the whole update (S13).
rules.description: Older OTAs: 6.14 mmap regression, Vulkan broken on 580.95.05, CX-7 power fixes, OOM handling (580.159.03).

rules.title: DGX Dashboard / fwupd Unhealthy
rules.trigger: DGX OS AND (dgx-dashboard.service or dgx-dashboard-admin.service inactive OR 127.0.0.1:11000 closed OR fwupd.service failed / 'libfwupd version X does not match daemon Y' OR >3 lingering check_ota_status.py)
rules.evidence_template: dgx-dashboard {s1}, dgx-dashboard-admin {s2}, port 11000 {open}, fwupd {fw} ('{err}'), {n} stuck check_ota_status.py.
rules.why_it_matters: The Dashboard is the primary update path; a hung fwupd makes Updates spin forever.
next_steps: Read-only: systemctl status dgx-dashboard dgx-dashboard-admin fwupd; fwupdmgr --version.

Advisory: sudo apt install --only-upgrade fwupd && sudo systemctl restart fwupd dgx-dashboard dgx-dashboard-admin (package upgrade plus service restarts; a restart interrupts an in-progress Dashboard update, so wait for one to finish; the services come back at boot, no revert needed).
rules.description: The Dashboard is the primary update path; a hung fwupd makes Updates spin forever.

rules.title: DGX Spark Firmware Behind the Current Release
rules.trigger: fwupdmgr get-devices, versions parsed from dotted (3.5.8) or hex (0x03000508) form and hex form decoded as major(8 bits).minor(16 bits).patch(8 bits) (0x03000508 = 3.5.8, 0x02009b0b = 2.155.11, 0x00000516 = 0.5.22 - arithmetic, unconfirmed against fwupdmgr output; assumption pending an fwupdmgr capture, and the fwupd device carrying the 2.155.11 SoC threshold must be confirmed). Founders Edition only (DMI sys_vendor NVIDIA): EC < 3.5.8, UEFI/SoC < 2.155.11, USB PD < 0.5.22 (S4 July 2026 table). OEM units (ASUS, HP, Lenovo, Dell, MSI, Acer, Gigabyte run their own firmware tracks): report only pending capsules from fwupdmgr get-upgrades, no threshold. The v1 'pre-production 5.36_0ACUM018' INFO variant is dropped: only S48 calls that SBIOS pre-production, in a 2x2 anecdotal sample, while 3.1 row 10 lists it as a normal FE BIOS.
rules.evidence_template: EC {ec}, UEFI/SoC {soc}, USB-PD {pd}, SBIOS {sbios} ({vendor}); FE reference 3.5.8 / 2.155.11 / 0.5.22 (July 2026, S4); pending {pending}.
rules.why_it_matters: 2026 firmware waves target USB-PD and EC stability; NVIDIA staff in S46 recommend current firmware plus a cold power cycle for the power-limited state (some users report it fixed; one user in S110 reports EC 3.5.8 worsened fan ramping).
next_steps: sudo fwupdmgr refresh && sudo fwupdmgr get-upgrades (read-only).

Advisory: apply firmware via the DGX Dashboard or your vendor channel, then cold power-cycle with the PSU unplugged; a firmware flash cannot be undone by NVCheckup and a downgrade is only sometimes offered (fwupdmgr downgrade, S110); check fwupdmgr get-history for 'Update State: Success'.
rules.description: 2026 firmware waves target USB-PD and EC stability; NVIDIA staff in S46 recommend current firmware plus a cold power cycle for the power-limited state (some users report it fixed; one user in S110 reports EC 3.5.8 worsened fan ramping).

rules.title: GB10 Power-Limited (USB-C PD wedge signature)
rules.trigger: GB10 AND in every thermal sample of the run: utilization.gpu >= 90 AND clocks.sm < 1400 MHz (typically 513/611/650/721) AND power.draw < 40 W AND all clock event reasons Not Active (thresholds from the community checker S120: >= 1400 MHz and >= 40 W sustained for 30 s passes). CRIT only when the signature persists across all samples; a single matching sample is WARN (a brief DVFS transition or a light memory-bound kernel can match once).
rules.evidence_template: Under load: {clk} MHz (max 3003), {util}%, {power} W, {temp} C, {pstate}; reasons Not Active in {n_match}/{n_samples} samples; SW Power Capping counter {us} us. Community-observed healthy range ~2200-2600 MHz at 80-100 W (S47, S108).
rules.why_it_matters: Community-observed signature (S46 forum thread; S47/S120 community repos; S6/S108/S123 threads) of a wedged USB-C PD contract: the SoC sits in a ~13-30 W fallback, 3-5x slower, -lgc has no effect and a warm reboot does not clear it. NVIDIA support in S46 confirmed the cold power cycle as the recovery and pointed a persistent OEM case to RMA (S107).
next_steps: Cold drain (no software change): shut down, unplug the PSU from wall AND unit, unplug all USB-C, hold power 30 s, wait 60 s, reconnect only the supplied adapter, re-test under load.
If it recurs: sudo nvidia-bug-report.sh and open a support/RMA case (NVIDIA for FE, the OEM for OEM units).
Advisory: update firmware via the DGX Dashboard or your vendor channel (firmware flashes cannot be rolled back), cold-drain again, and avoid suspend/resume (S51).
rules.description: Community-observed signature (S46 forum thread; S47/S120 community repos; S6/S108/S123 threads) of a wedged USB-C PD contract: the SoC sits in a ~13-30 W fallback, 3-5x slower, -lgc has no effect and a warm reboot does not clear it. NVIDIA support in S46 confirmed the cold power cycle as the recovery and pointed a persistent OEM case to RMA (S107).

rules.title: Log-less Hard Power-Off on GB10
rules.trigger: GB10 AND the previous boot's journal (journalctl -b -1) ends without a clean-shutdown marker - 'systemd-journald: Journal stopped', 'systemd-shutdown', 'Shutting down.', 'Reached target Power-Off' / 'Reboot' / 'Halt' (the kernel's 'reboot: Power down' is printed after journald has stopped and normally never lands in the journal) - AND no panic/OOM/Xid/thermal lines AND /sys/fs/pstore empty. WARN only when >= 2 such unclean boots occurred in the last {days} days (default 14); one unclean boot is INFO. Mains loss and power-button holds leave the same signature and are named as alternative explanations.
rules.evidence_template: {n} boots without a clean-shutdown marker in {days} days; last line of boot -1 '{line}'; pstore empty; max SM clock {max_clock}; EC {ec}, SBIOS {sbios}. Alternative explanations: mains loss, power-button hold.
rules.why_it_matters: Community reports (S48 repo, S105 thread) describe the EC cutting power under ~90 W sustained GPU load before the kernel can log; S48 quotes NVIDIA staff calling it 'a known issue' with a clock cap as the workaround, and RMAs were granted for fieldiag PowerStress failures (MODS-020000610139, S106). These are community reports, not an NVIDIA statement.
next_steps: Use the supplied 240 W adapter directly in the wall, unstack, keep ambient 5-30 C (S20); reduce memory over-commit (same signature).
Advisory: update firmware via the DGX Dashboard, then cold power-cycle (firmware flashes cannot be rolled back).

Advisory: (community mitigation from S48, never applied by NVCheckup) sudo nvidia-smi -lgc 300,2200 caps clocks at a ~1-10% throughput cost (S48 estimates 1-5%) and does not persist across reboot unless you add a systemd unit; revert with sudo nvidia-smi -rgc.

Advisory: (fieldiag, S16) sudo apt install dgx-spark-fieldiag; partnerdiag requires Secure Boot disabled in UEFI setup (Security > Secure Boot) - re-enable it afterwards; sudo init 3 ends the graphical session (save work first; a reboot restores it); then sudo /opt/nvidia/dgx-spark-fieldiag/partnerdiag --field.
rules.description: Community reports (S48 repo, S105 thread) describe the EC cutting power under ~90 W sustained GPU load before the kernel can log; S48 quotes NVIDIA staff calling it 'a known issue' with a clock cap as the workaround, and RMAs were granted for fieldiag PowerStress failures (MODS-020000610139, S106). These are community reports, not an NVIDIA statement.

rules.title: GB10 ACPI Thermal Zone Hot
rules.trigger: GB10 AND any acpitz zone >= 93000 mC (inference from community reports: a 93.1 C SoC zone ~2 min before a hard freeze in S106, 96-97 C zones with quiet fans in S49/S110, 88->97.8 C in 5 s before a shutdown in S109), or SW/HW Thermal Slowdown counters > 0 below the thermal-throttling thresholds.
rules.evidence_template: ACPI zones {zones} (max {mc} mC) vs GPU {gpu_temp} C; slowdown counters SW {sw} / HW {hw} us; fan telemetry unavailable (EC); EC {ec}.
rules.why_it_matters: A single thread (S49) reports a package sensor up to ~20 C above the GPU reading; 96-97 C zones with quiet fans preceded hard power-offs in S49/S109/S110 (community reports).
next_steps: Improve airflow: unstack, unblock vents, ambient 5-30 C (S20); read-only: fwupdmgr get-devices for the EC level.
OEM units: contact the OEM (own firmware track).

Advisory: (fieldiag, S16) partnerdiag requires Secure Boot disabled in UEFI setup - re-enable it afterwards; sudo init 3 ends the graphical session; then sudo /opt/nvidia/dgx-spark-fieldiag/partnerdiag --field.
rules.description: A single thread (S49) reports a package sensor up to ~20 C above the GPU reading; 96-97 C zones with quiet fans preceded hard power-offs in S49/S109/S110 (community reports).

rules.title: GB10 Clock Cap Active
rules.trigger: GB10 AND (gb10-clock-cap.service exists OR 'Applications Clocks Setting: Active' OR locked max SM clock < 3003 MHz)
rules.evidence_template: Clocks locked to {min}-{max} MHz (hardware max 3003) via {source}; community estimates ~1-10% throughput cost (S48).
rules.why_it_matters: Explains lower clocks so they are not mistaken for throttling; does not fix the PD wedge.
next_steps: No action if you set the cap deliberately (S48 community mitigation).

Advisory: sudo nvidia-smi -rgc removes the cap only if you set it and no longer want it (revert: re-run your -lgc command). A gb10-clock-cap.service unit re-applies it at boot: sudo systemctl disable --now gb10-clock-cap.service (revert: sudo systemctl enable --now gb10-clock-cap.service).
rules.description: Explains lower clocks so they are not mistaken for throttling; does not fix the PD wedge.

rules.title: Suspend/Resume Failure on DGX Spark
rules.trigger: GB10 AND journal 'PM: suspend entry (s2idle)' AND ('WARNING: ... at nvidia/nv.c' together with 'nv_set_system_power_state' - no line number, it changes with every driver build - OR nvidia-suspend.service failed); also headless units whose GDM greeter sleep-inactive-ac-type != 'nothing' (S52, S127).
rules.evidence_template: {n} suspend attempts; driver {driver} logged nv_set_system_power_state warning / nvidia-suspend.service failed; GDM greeter policy {policy}.
rules.why_it_matters: Suspend is disabled by default on Spark and s2idle does not complete; resume triggers the PD wedge; headless boxes suspend from the login screen and drop Wi-Fi.
next_steps: Keep suspend off: GNOME Settings > Power > Automatic Suspend = Off (reversible in the same dialog).
Re-test clocks after any suspend (gb10-pd-power-wedge).
Advisory: sudo systemctl mask sleep.target suspend.target (persistent; revert: sudo systemctl unmask sleep.target suspend.target).

Advisory: (headless, S52) sudo -u gdm dbus-run-session gsettings set org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power sleep-inactive-ac-type 'nothing' (persistent; revert: sudo -u gdm dbus-run-session gsettings reset org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power sleep-inactive-ac-type).
rules.description: Suspend is disabled by default on Spark and s2idle does not complete; resume triggers the PD wedge; headless boxes suspend from the login screen and drop Wi-Fi.

rules.title: ConnectX-7 Slot Power Message Is Benign
rules.trigger: --include-logs AND dmesg 'mlx5_core ... Detected insufficient power on the PCIe slot (27W)' or correctable AER on the ConnectX-7
rules.evidence_template: dmesg '{line}': benign per NVIDIA moderators (no slot power limit advertised).
rules.why_it_matters: Prevents a false power fault; only fatal AER or a ~13 Gb/s link matters.
next_steps: Ignore unless gb10-pd-power-wedge or cx7-link-speed-degraded also fires.
rules.description: Prevents a false power fault; only fatal AER or a ~13 Gb/s link matters.

rules.title: CUDA 12 Wheel on a CUDA 13 Host
rules.trigger: WARN: torch.version.cuda 12.x / wheel tag +cu12x on a CUDA 13-only host (cu12x wheels bundle their own CUDA 12 runtime via nvidia-*-cu12 and are driver-compatible with R580, but may lack sm_121 kernels). CRIT only when the import error 'libcudart.so.12: cannot open shared object file' / 'libnvrtc.so.12' is observed.
rules.evidence_template: {package} {version} is built for CUDA {pkg_cuda}; host has CUDA {host_cuda} ({missing_lib} {present_or_absent}). Tag-only finding: may lack sm_121 kernels; verify torch.cuda.is_available() and a matmul.
rules.why_it_matters: A cu12 wheel may import yet miss sm_121 kernels (sm121-kernel-missing) or fail to import when it expects a system libcudart.so.12; a frequent GB10 setup failure (S33 and S118 community setup guides).
next_steps: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 (reversible: reinstall the previous wheel); vLLM +cu130 aarch64 wheel or https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/cu130; SGLang lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130.
Remove stray nvidia-*-cu12 pip packages from the venv (reversible: pip install them again).
rules.description: A cu12 wheel may import yet miss sm_121 kernels (sm121-kernel-missing) or fail to import when it expects a system libcudart.so.12; a frequent GB10 setup failure (S33 and S118 community setup guides).

rules.title: PyTorch Capability 12.1 Warning Is Benign
rules.trigger: torch probe stderr 'Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1. Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)' or arch list has sm_120 but not sm_121
rules.evidence_template: PyTorch {version} (CUDA {torch_cuda}) warns about capability 12.1; arch list {arch_list}. sm_120 SASS runs on sm_121.
rules.why_it_matters: Stops users rebuilding PyTorch for sm_121 or blaming the warning for unrelated failures.
next_steps: No action; confirm torch.version.cuda starts with 13 and a matmul runs on cuda.
rules.description: Stops users rebuilding PyTorch for sm_121 or blaming the warning for unrelated failures.

rules.title: No sm_121 Kernels for GB10/N1X
rules.trigger: CC 12.1 AND (logs 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device', 'kernel built for sm80-sm100, but running on sm121', 'cudaErrorSymbolNotFound', 'TRTLLMGenFusedMoE does not support SM120 and above' OR torch arch list lacks sm_120/sm_121/compute_120)
rules.evidence_template: {component} has no sm_120/sm_120f/sm_121a kernels: '{line}'. GB10/N1X are CC 12.1; sm_100 and sm_90 binaries never run here.
rules.why_it_matters: Kernel launches fail or fall back to slow generic paths: a vLLM build without native sm_121 cubins gave 13 tok/s vs 48.6 tok/s after rebuild (~4x, single measurement, S54).
next_steps: Use cu130 aarch64 wheels or NGC images with sm_121 (pytorch >= 25.10, vllm 26.xx, tensorrt-llm >= 1.2); rebuild with TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1+PTX" (sm_120 SASS also runs on 12.1, S53/S119) or CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121a-real for llama.cpp; verify cuobjdump --list-elf <lib.so> | grep -c sm_12 (all reversible: reinstall the previous wheel).
rules.description: Kernel launches fail or fall back to slow generic paths: a vLLM build without native sm_121 cubins gave 13 tok/s vs 48.6 tok/s after rebuild (~4x, single measurement, S54).

rules.title: Triton Bundles a Stale ptxas (no sm_121a)
rules.trigger: triton installed AND (bundled ptxas < 13.0 AND TRITON_PTXAS_PATH unset) OR logs "ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_121a' is not defined for option 'gpu-name'"
rules.evidence_template: Triton {tv} bundles ptxas {pv}; TRITON_PTXAS_PATH={val}; system ptxas {sys}. Error '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: torch.compile, FlashInfer/Triton attention and TRT-LLM NVFP4 kernels JIT at runtime and abort.
next_steps: export TRITON_PTXAS_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas (mpirun -x TRITON_PTXAS_PATH for TRT-LLM); TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1+PTX" (environment only, reversible).
rules.description: torch.compile, FlashInfer/Triton attention and TRT-LLM NVFP4 kernels JIT at runtime and abort.

rules.title: flash_attn Has No aarch64 Wheel
rules.trigger: aarch64 AND pip has flash_attn / vllm-flash-attn (or Transformers 'FlashAttention2 has been toggled on, but flash_attn is not installed')
rules.evidence_template: flash_attn {version} on aarch64: no official linux_aarch64+sm121 wheels exist (S55).
rules.why_it_matters: Import errors break attn_implementation='flash_attention_2'; community guidance for Blackwell consumer parts (S33, S55) is SDPA.
next_steps: pip uninstall flash-attn; use attn_implementation="sdpa" or the NGC container's bundled kernels (reversible).

If FA2 is required, build from source targeting 12.1: TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="12.1+PTX" FLASH_ATTENTION_FORCE_BUILD=TRUE (the one arch recommendation, shared with sm121-kernel-missing; if the build script rejects 12.1, the sm_120 build FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS="120" also runs on 12.1, S119).
rules.description: Import errors break attn_implementation='flash_attention_2'; community guidance for Blackwell consumer parts (S33, S55) is SDPA.

rules.title: amd64 Container Image on an arm64 Host
rules.trigger: docker image inspect Architecture == amd64 on aarch64, or container logs 'exec format error'
rules.evidence_template: Image {image} is linux/amd64; host is linux/arm64.
rules.why_it_matters: The container cannot start and users blame the GPU/driver.
next_steps: Pull an arm64 tag (docker manifest inspect must list linux/arm64); check the DGX Spark Collection on NGC before pulling NIMs.
rules.description: The container cannot start and users blame the GPU/driver.

rules.title: NGC Image Predates CUDA 13 / sm_121
rules.trigger: images include nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch <= 25.09 (the DGX Spark NGC doc page still recommended 24.08-py3 at research time, S112), nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorflow (NVIDIA-optimized TensorFlow reached EOL after 25.02, S113), lmsysorg/sglang:latest (cu12, S94), or tensorrt-llm/release < 1.2
rules.evidence_template: {image} predates CUDA 13 / sm_121 (25.08 was the first CUDA 13 NGC PyTorch and the playbooks pin 25.11-py3, S114; 25.10 is the first tag observed shipping compute_120 for GB10, S118).
rules.why_it_matters: nvidia-smi works inside but torch.cuda.is_available() is False or kernels fail.
next_steps: Use nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.11-py3+, nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:26.05-py3, tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc13, lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130; pin tags (pulling a newer image is reversible).
rules.description: nvidia-smi works inside but torch.cuda.is_available() is False or kernels fail.

rules.title: Snap Docker Cannot Use the GPU
rules.trigger: snap list docker succeeds, or error 'nvidia-container-cli: initialization error: load library failed: libnvidia-ml.so.1'
rules.evidence_template: Snap Docker {ver} installed; docker-ce {state}; error '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Snap-confined Docker cannot load host NVML; the DGX OS recipe (NVIDIA moderator in S58) is docker-ce plus nv-docker-gpus / nv-docker-options.
next_steps: Advisory: (data loss) sudo snap remove docker deletes the snap's containers, images and volumes; first export what you need (docker save / docker export) or sudo snap save docker to keep a snapshot restorable with snap restore.
Advisory: sudo apt install docker-ce docker-ce-cli docker-compose-plugin nv-docker-gpus nv-docker-options (S58; package install, revert: apt remove them).
rules.description: Snap-confined Docker cannot load host NVML; the DGX OS recipe (NVIDIA moderator in S58) is docker-ce plus nv-docker-gpus / nv-docker-options.

rules.title: Docker CDI Spec / nvidia Runtime Missing
rules.trigger: daemon.json enables CDI AND no /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml or /var/run/cdi/nvidia.yaml (or logs 'no nvidia.com/gpu CDI spec is present on the host'); INFO variant when daemon.json lacks runtimes.nvidia ('unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia')
rules.evidence_template: Docker CDI {cdi}, nvidia.yaml {present}, runtimes {runtimes} (toolkit {ctk}); error '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Factory images (toolkit 1.19.0) shipped without the CDI spec unit; --gpus all works without the named runtime, compose files using runtime: nvidia do not.
next_steps: Advisory: sudo nvidia-ctk cdi generate --output=/etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml writes a new file (revert: sudo rm /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml).

Advisory: sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker edits /etc/docker/daemon.json (back it up first; revert by restoring the copy), and sudo systemctl restart docker stops every running container unless live-restore is enabled - do it between jobs.
rules.description: Factory images (toolkit 1.19.0) shipped without the CDI spec unit; --gpus all works without the named runtime, compose files using runtime: nvidia do not.

rules.title: onnxruntime Has No CUDAExecutionProvider
rules.trigger: onnxruntime importable AND 'CUDAExecutionProvider' not in get_available_providers() (both onnxruntime and onnxruntime-gpu installed, or PyPI CPU wheel on aarch64)
rules.evidence_template: Providers {providers}; onnxruntime={v1}, onnxruntime-gpu={v2}. No prebuilt onnxruntime-gpu wheels for aarch64 Linux existed as of April 2026 (S61); a later pip install of the CPU wheel shadows a GPU build.
rules.why_it_matters: ONNX-backed pipelines run on CPU with no error.
next_steps: Advisory: pip uninstall onnxruntime (reversible); install a community sm_121 onnxruntime-gpu build or build ORT 1.27+ (CUDA 13.0 + cuDNN 9) with --cmake_extra_defines CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 after sudo apt install libcudnn9-cuda-13 libcudnn9-dev-cuda-13 (package install; S61) (revert: sudo apt remove libcudnn9-cuda-13 libcudnn9-dev-cuda-13).
rules.description: ONNX-backed pipelines run on CPU with no error.

rules.title: Kubernetes Device Plugin Too Old for GB10
rules.trigger: kubectl present AND device plugin < v0.17.4 (DRA driver < v0.4.0, HAMi <= 2.7.1) or pod logs 'error getting device memory: Not Supported'
rules.evidence_template: {plugin} {version} on GB10: '{line}'; nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo returns NVML_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED on unified memory (S8; HAMi S116).
rules.why_it_matters: Node advertises zero nvidia.com/gpu (CrashLoopBackOff); one S8 comment (2026-03-31) reports MPS also failing ('getpwuid() failed for 0') so only time-slicing worked (single report).
next_steps: Advisory: (cluster-wide change) upgrade k8s-device-plugin >= v0.17.4 / dra-driver >= v0.4.0 / HAMi with preConfiguredDeviceMemory (revert: helm rollback <release>); do not rely on the gpu.memory label.
rules.description: Node advertises zero nvidia.com/gpu (CrashLoopBackOff); one S8 comment (2026-03-31) reports MPS also failing ('getpwuid() failed for 0') so only time-slicing worked (single report).

rules.title: ConnectX-7 Not Enumerated
rules.trigger: GB10 AND no PCI 15b3 devices AND dmesg 'cx7-pcie-hotplug MTKP0001:00: Cable removal' or 'broken device, retraining non-functional downstream link at 2.5GT/s'; WARN variant when kernel is 6.17.0-1021-nvidia or 6.17.0-1029-nvidia even if the NIC is present
rules.evidence_template: ConnectX-7 not enumerated: {count} 15b3 devices; kernel {kernel}; dmesg '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: No 200 Gb/s link, RoCE or multi-node NCCL; 6.17.0-1021/1029-nvidia have a hotplug regression that drops the NIC 5-22 s after boot, retraining failures needed RMA.
next_steps: Cold power cycle with power and QSFP unplugged (no software change).
Persistent 'retraining failed' -> fieldiag (Advisory: partnerdiag needs Secure Boot disabled in UEFI setup, re-enable it afterwards) and RMA.

Advisory: on 6.17.0-1021/1029-nvidia move to the fixed 6.17 kernel (>= 6.17.0-1031-nvidia, spec 2.1) via the DGX Dashboard or apt (kernel change; revert by selecting the previous entry in GRUB). Pinning linux-image-6.14.0-1015-nvidia plus matching nvidia-580-open modules is a stop-gap kernel downgrade only: it makes dgx-spark-ota-outdated fire (revert: apt-mark unhold and reinstall the current kernel).
rules.description: No 200 Gb/s link, RoCE or multi-node NCCL; 6.17.0-1021/1029-nvidia have a hotplug regression that drops the NIC 5-22 s after boot, retraining failures needed RMA.

rules.title: ConnectX-7 Twin Link State Mismatch
rules.trigger: within one cage (functions .0 of PCI domains 0000 and 0002 = port 0; .1 = port 1) one twin ACTIVE and the other DOWN, or dmesg 'QSFP module not powered' / 'Cable unplugged'
rules.evidence_template: Port {port}: {twin_a} {state_a} but {twin_b} {state_b}; /etc/nvidia/cx7-hotplug-enabled {present}.
rules.why_it_matters: Each cage is two 100 Gb/s PCIe x4 twins; one twin down caps the link at ~100 Gb/s; the Jan-2026 hot-plug power file can keep lanes from training.
next_steps: Reseat an approved DAC (Amphenol NJAAKK-N911/NJAAKK0006, Luxshare LMTQF022-SD-R, S17); reboot both nodes with the cable attached (no configuration change).

Advisory: (community workaround from S63, not NVIDIA guidance) if lanes never train, sudo rm -f /etc/nvidia/cx7-hotplug-enabled on both nodes and reboot; restore the NVIDIA-managed file with sudo touch /etc/nvidia/cx7-hotplug-enabled and reboot.
rules.description: Each cage is two 100 Gb/s PCIe x4 twins; one twin down caps the link at ~100 Gb/s; the Jan-2026 hot-plug power file can keep lanes from training.

rules.title: ConnectX-7 Link Speed Degraded
rules.trigger: an Up CX-7 twin reports /sys/class/net/<if>/speed != 200000
rules.evidence_template: {iface} negotiated {speed} Mb/s; expected 200000; CX-7 firmware {fw}.
rules.why_it_matters: A 100G cable/switch port or firmware regression halves NCCL bandwidth; the ~13 Gb/s state needs a reboot with the cable attached or firmware + cold drain.
next_steps: Use a >= 200 Gb/s cable; switch ports at 200G, autoneg off, one L2 bridge, MTU 9000 (switch-side settings, outside this host); sudo fwupdmgr get-upgrades (read-only).
rules.description: A 100G cable/switch port or firmware regression halves NCCL bandwidth; the ~13 Gb/s state needs a reboot with the cable attached or firmware + cold drain.

rules.title: ConnectX-7 Port Up Without an IPv4 Address
rules.trigger: a CX-7 twin is ACTIVE/Up with no IPv4, or its address is not persisted in netplan/NM (INFO)
rules.evidence_template: {iface} ({rdma_dev}) Up at {speed} Mb/s; IPv4 {ip}; persistent config {persistent}.
rules.why_it_matters: NCCL and discover-sparks cannot use an unaddressed link; ip addr add is lost at reboot; with two cables all four twins need addresses.
next_steps: Advisory: write /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml (chmod 600) with dhcp4: no and a static address per twin, then sudo netplan apply (persistent network change; revert: sudo rm /etc/netplan/40-cx7.yaml && sudo netplan apply) (S18).
rules.description: NCCL and discover-sparks cannot use an unaddressed link; ip addr add is lost at reboot; with two cables all four twins need addresses.

rules.title: ConnectX-7 Twins Share a Subnet or Bond
rules.trigger: both twins of a cage carry IPv4 addresses in the same subnet, or a twin is enslaved to a Linux bond
rules.evidence_template: {twin_a}={ip_a} and {twin_b}={ip_b} share {subnet}; bond {bond}.
rules.why_it_matters: Same-subnet or bonded twins break routing/ARP, RoCE reachability and NCCL autodiscovery ('Interfaces X and Y share the same subnet').
next_steps: Advisory: one /24 per twin on both nodes (192.168.100.x / 192.168.101.x) in netplan and remove bonds (persistent network change; revert by restoring the previous netplan file and sudo netplan apply) (S65); list both twins in NCCL_IB_HCA.
rules.description: Same-subnet or bonded twins break routing/ARP, RoCE reachability and NCCL autodiscovery ('Interfaces X and Y share the same subnet').

rules.title: ConnectX-7 MTU Mismatch
rules.trigger: MTU differs between twins of a cage, or an addressed twin is 1500 while netplan/peer uses 9000
rules.evidence_template: MTU {twin_a}={a}, {twin_b}={b}; netplan mtu {np}.
rules.why_it_matters: Silent jumbo-frame drops; a 3-node NCCL failure and the 3 GB/s plateau were traced to 1500 vs 9000.
next_steps: Advisory: mtu: 9000 on all twins on every node in netplan (persistent; revert: remove the mtu key and sudo netplan apply); switch l2mtu 9216; verify with ping -M do -s 8972 <peer> (read-only).
rules.description: Silent jumbo-frame drops; a 3-node NCCL failure and the 3 GB/s plateau were traced to 1500 vs 9000.

rules.title: NCCL Environment Misconfigured for DGX Spark
rules.trigger: CX-7 twins Up AND (NCCL_IB_HCA names a netdev, lists one twin of a cage, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1, an NCCL net plugin present without NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none, libnccl.so.2 < 2.28, 3+ nodes without NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1, or a supplied log shows 'Using network Socket' / 'ibv_modify_qp failed with 110')
rules.evidence_template: NCCL_IB_HCA={hca}; NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME={ifname}; NCCL_IB_DISABLE={dis}; NCCL_NET_PLUGIN={plugin} (lib {lib}); libnccl {ver}; log '{line}'.
rules.why_it_matters: Each misstep drops the pair from ~22-24 GB/s busbw to ~12 GB/s (one twin) or 1-3 GB/s (sockets); NCCL < 2.28 lacks sm_121 and hangs.
next_steps: export NCCL_IB_HCA={active_twins} - both twins of the cabled cage as the collector saw them ACTIVE (port 0: rocep1s0f0,roceP2p1s0f0; port 1: rocep1s0f1,roceP2p1s0f1) - NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME={cabled_netdev} NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3 NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none; rings: NCCL_IB_SUBNET_AWARE_ROUTING=1 NCCL_IB_MERGE_NICS=0 (environment only, reversible).

NCCL < 2.28 lacks sm_121 support and collectives hang (community benchmark S102; stock NGC 2.27.7): build NCCL v2.30.7-1 with -gencode=arch=compute_121,code=sm_121 per the NVIDIA playbook (S67); confirm 'NET/IB' in NCCL_DEBUG=INFO.
rules.description: Each misstep drops the pair from ~22-24 GB/s busbw to ~12 GB/s (one twin) or 1-3 GB/s (sockets); NCCL < 2.28 lacks sm_121 and hangs.

rules.title: GPUDirect RDMA Assumed (unsupported on Spark)
rules.trigger: NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL set (not 0/LOC) or NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=1, or dmesg 'nvidia_peermem: Unknown symbol ib_register_peer_memory_client'
rules.evidence_template: {var}={value}; nvidia_peermem load attempted {attempted}. NCCL logs 'GPU Direct RDMA Disabled for HCA' / 'GDR 0' on Spark.
rules.why_it_matters: GPUDirect RDMA, nvidia-peermem, dma-buf and GDRCopy are unsupported (cudaMalloc memory is not CPU/PCIe coherent); assuming GDR causes init hangs.
next_steps: NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=0, NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=0 (environment only, reversible); do not install nvidia-peermem/GDRCopy; RDMA buffers via cudaHostAlloc + ib_reg_mr (S69).
rules.description: GPUDirect RDMA, nvidia-peermem, dma-buf and GDRCopy are unsupported (cudaMalloc memory is not CPU/PCIe coherent); assuming GDR causes init hangs.

rules.title: mDNS Hostname Conflict on the Cluster Fabric
rules.trigger: journalctl -u avahi-daemon 'Host name conflict, retrying with' or hostname with -2/-3 suffix; INFO variant when twins are Up but avahi-daemon/avahi-browse are absent
rules.evidence_template: avahi {state}: renamed host to {new_name} ('{line}'); avahi-utils {pkg}.
rules.why_it_matters: Cabled twins without DHCP flap and avahi sees its own announcements as conflicts; spark-xxxx.local becomes unreachable for NVIDIA Sync and discover-sparks needs avahi-browse.
next_steps: Advisory: static addresses on the twins (netplan dhcp4: no; persistent, revert by restoring the previous netplan and sudo netplan apply).
Advisory: sudo apt-get install -y avahi-utils (package install; revert: apt remove avahi-utils).
Advisory: sudo systemctl restart avahi-daemon (brief mDNS outage; no revert needed).
rules.description: Cabled twins without DHCP flap and avahi sees its own announcements as conflicts; spark-xxxx.local becomes unreachable for NVIDIA Sync and discover-sparks needs avahi-browse.

rules.title: Firewall Blocks Cluster Traffic
rules.trigger: CX-7 twins addressed AND ufw enabled (/etc/ufw/ufw.conf ENABLED=yes) without allow rules for the fabric subnets or 5353/udp, 22/tcp, 29500/tcp
rules.evidence_template: ufw {state}, default {policy}; no rule for {missing} on {subnets}.
rules.why_it_matters: Blocks mDNS discovery, mpirun SSH launch and torch.distributed rendezvous ('Watchdog caught collective operation timeout').
next_steps: Advisory: sudo ufw allow from <fabric-subnet>/24 (both twins) or at least sudo ufw allow 29500/tcp, 5353/udp, 22/tcp (persistent firewall change; revert: sudo ufw status numbered then sudo ufw delete <n>, or sudo ufw delete allow from <fabric-subnet>/24).
rules.description: Blocks mDNS discovery, mpirun SSH launch and torch.distributed rendezvous ('Watchdog caught collective operation timeout').

rules.title: RTX Spark Developer Preview Driver
rules.trigger: RTX Spark AND (INF nv_surface_woa.inf OR driver 616.00 (WDDM DriverVersion ending 16.1600; the full 32.0.16.1600 string is unconfirmed) OR package name DeveloperPreview OR driver < 616.00 on ARM64)
rules.evidence_template: Driver {version} ({inf}) is the RTX Spark Developer Preview branch (R616, 2026-07-16, S24); below 616.00 on Arm64 is an extracted/unofficial build.
rules.why_it_matters: NVIDIA lists the preview stack as pre-release, not for production or benchmarking (S26 release notes), with the known issue 'Possible system instability during PyTorch build workflows' (S24 landing page). (The v1 '~2 min blank display during install' claim had no source and was dropped.)
next_steps: Check the RTX Spark Developer Preview thread (S24) and OEM/Windows Update for a production Arm64 driver (read-only).
Advisory: installing a different driver replaces the Developer Preview package (revert: reinstall the 616.00 DP package from the S24 thread).
rules.description: NVIDIA lists the preview stack as pre-release, not for production or benchmarking (S26 release notes), with the known issue 'Possible system instability during PyTorch build workflows' (S24 landing page). (The v1 '~2 min blank display during install' claim had no source and was dropped.)

rules.title: CUDA Toolkit Is Not Native Windows Arm64
rules.trigger: Windows ARM64 AND CUDA toolkit whose nvcc.exe PE machine is AMD64 (0x8664) or version <= 13.3
rules.evidence_template: CUDA {version} at {CUDA_PATH} is x86_64 under Prism; the first native Windows Arm64 toolkit is 13.4 Developer Preview.
rules.why_it_matters: An emulated toolkit targets x64 and cannot exercise the native Arm64 CUDA runtime.
next_steps: Install CUDA 13.4 DP (Windows ARM64) or cross-compile from x86_64 (toolkit install, reversible via Settings > Apps); use pinned host memory (S26 documents a pageable-memory slowdown).
rules.description: An emulated toolkit targets x64 and cannot exercise the native Arm64 CUDA runtime.

rules.title: NVCheckup Running Under x64 Emulation (Prism)
rules.trigger: IsWow64Process2 native machine IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_ARM64 (0xAA64) AND process machine != IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_UNKNOWN
rules.evidence_template: NVCheckup runs under Prism (process {proc}, host ARM64); CPU data reflects the emulated processor.
rules.why_it_matters: Emulated processes get emulated CPU details and registry/filesystem redirection.
next_steps: Run nvcheckup-windows-arm64.exe.
rules.description: Emulated processes get emulated CPU details and registry/filesystem redirection.

rules.title: Windows Build Too Old for RTX Spark
rules.trigger: Windows ARM64 AND BuildNumber < 26100
rules.evidence_template: Windows build {build} predates 24H2 (26100); RTX Spark devices are expected to ship 26H1 (build 28000, device-scoped, S74) or newer per the launch announcement (S27) - unconfirmed.
rules.why_it_matters: Prism AVX/AVX2 emulation (S73) and downloadable Windows ML execution providers incl. NvTensorRtRtx (S115) require 24H2 (26100) or later.
next_steps: Advisory: update Windows to 24H2 or later via Settings > Windows Update (feature update; Windows keeps a 10-day rollback under Settings > System > Recovery); 26H1 is device-scoped, not an in-place update (S74).
rules.description: Prism AVX/AVX2 emulation (S73) and downloadable Windows ML execution providers incl. NvTensorRtRtx (S115) require 24H2 (26100) or later.

rules.title: Linux NVIDIA Driver Installed Inside WSL
rules.trigger: inside WSL2 AND dpkg/rpm lists nvidia-driver-* / nvidia-dkms-*, or /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so missing while the Windows driver is present. On RTX Spark this applies where WSL2 GPU passthrough exists: announced for the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box (S122); NVIDIA's WSL guide (S75) covers x86_64 hosts only, so other Arm devices are unconfirmed.
rules.evidence_template: WSL distro {distro} ({arch}) has Linux NVIDIA driver packages {pkgs}; /usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so {present}.
rules.why_it_matters: CUDA in WSL comes from the Windows driver; NVIDIA: 'users must not install any NVIDIA GPU Linux driver within WSL 2'.
next_steps: Advisory: remove the in-distro driver packages (sudo apt purge 'nvidia-driver-*' 'nvidia-dkms-*'; revert: reinstall them, although NVIDIA says they must not be installed inside WSL, S75).
Advisory: update the Windows driver (>= 616.00 on RTX Spark; host driver change, revert: reinstall the previous package); use aarch64 cu130 wheels in an aarch64 distro.
rules.description: CUDA in WSL comes from the Windows driver; NVIDIA: 'users must not install any NVIDIA GPU Linux driver within WSL 2'.

rules.title: RTX Spark (N1X) on Linux Is Unsupported
rules.trigger: Linux AND lspci [10de:2e03] or [10de:2e06]
rules.evidence_template: RTX Spark N1X [{pciid}] under Linux ({distro}, kernel {kernel}, driver {driver}); NVIDIA has not announced Linux support for RTX Spark as of {date} (S76 reports the absence of an announcement).
rules.why_it_matters: Closest reference is DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04, R580 open, CUDA 13.0, sm_121); laptop drivers unverified.
next_steps: Treat results as best-effort; expect nvidia-smi memory fields [N/A] as on GB10.
rules.description: Closest reference is DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04, R580 open, CUDA 13.0, sm_121); laptop drivers unverified.
